sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Technology and Financials stand out as the only two "all-green" sectors, while marginal rotations favor Financials and Healthcare at the expense of Real Estate and Consumer Defensive.

Technology (momentum 0.85) and Energy (momentum 0.72) continue to lead the market, with Technology joining Financials (momentum 0.63) as the only two sectors displaying "all-green" breadth across all timeframes. Financials and Healthcare (momentum 0.67) are the sole upward rotators this week, each gaining one spot in the rankings.

Conversely, defensive sectors are fading. Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.23) and Real Estate (momentum 0.40) both slipped one spot over the last five sessions. Utilities (momentum 0.13) and Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.23) remain anchored at the bottom of the momentum rankings, showing no signs of recovery.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 2 of 11 sectors—Technology (0.85 momentum) and Financials (0.63 momentum)—are positive across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD.
* **Top-Ranked Leaders:** Energy holds the #1 YTD rank with a strong 0.72 momentum score, followed closely by Technology at rank #2 and Basic Materials at rank #3 (0.80 momentum).

## Movers & Momentum
* **Positive Rotators:** Financials (rank 7) and Healthcare (rank 5) are the top gainers, each improving their rank by +1 spot over the last 5 sessions.
* **Defensive Slippage:** Consumer Defensive (rank 8, 0.23 momentum) and Real Estate (rank 6, 0.40 momentum) are the top losers, both dropping -1 spot.
* **Momentum Laggards:** Utilities (0.13 momentum, rank 9) and Consumer Cyclical (0.23 momentum, rank 11) remain heavily depressed at the bottom of the momentum spectrum.

## Divergences
* **No Fragile Leaders:** No fragile "all-green" sectors were detected, indicating that the multi-timeframe strength in Technology and Financials is currently stable.
* **Rank-to-Momentum Alignment:** High-momentum sectors like Basic Materials (0.80 momentum, rank 3) and Technology (0.85 momentum, rank 2) show strong alignment between their YTD rankings and current momentum.

rotation_phase.label: Mid Cycle
rotation_phase.reasoning: Technology and Basic Materials are leading momentum alongside strong breadth in Financials, which fits the Mid Cycle phase as growth and cyclical industries drive market performance.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Commodities and heavy energy dominate US industry leadership, led by Copper and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, while a massive weekly surge in Uranium and Coking Coal highlights a rotation into alternative energy and raw materials.

Market breadth remains highly selective with 27 of 143 industry groups holding "all-green" status across all timeframes. Copper (momentum 0.92) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.91) lead the momentum charge, backed by sustained strength in Biotechnology and Marine Shipping. Rotation is heavily favoring nuclear and fossil fuel inputs, with Uranium climbing 37 spots to rank 54 and Coking Coal jumping 29 spots to rank 45.

Conversely, consumer-facing and retail-adjacent sectors are fading rapidly. Apparel Manufacturing dropped 19 spots, REIT - Diversified fell 17 spots, and Specialty Retail lost 16 spots. Furthermore, some high-momentum energy segments are showing early signs of fatigue, as Oil & Gas Integrated and Oil & Gas E&P both slipped in rank despite holding decent momentum.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 27 of 143 industry groups maintain positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD windows.
* **Momentum Leaders:** Copper (0.918) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.913) sit at the top of the momentum curve, followed closely by Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.878) and Computer Hardware (0.858).
* **Sustained Strong:** Biotechnology, Marine Shipping, Health Information Services, and Software - Infrastructure are among the top 35 groups consistently performing across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Uranium surged +37 spots to rank 54 (momentum 0.63), while Coking Coal jumped +29 spots to rank 45 (momentum 0.83) and Department Stores improved by +20 spots to rank 91.
* **Top Losers:** Apparel Manufacturing plunged -19 spots to rank 106 (momentum 0.21), followed by REIT - Diversified (-17 spots to rank 103) and Specialty Retail (-16 spots to rank 93).
* **Momentum Laggards:** Footwear & Accessories (0.023) and Advertising Agencies (0.113) remain anchored at the bottom of the YTD rankings.

## Divergences
* **Fading Giants:** Rank slips over the last 5 sessions point to near-term exhaustion in high-momentum groups, including Oil & Gas Integrated (momentum 0.63, rank -7), Oil & Gas E&P (momentum 0.66, rank -6), and Drug Manufacturers - General (momentum 0.63, rank -5).
* **Emerging Groups:** Sectors climbing the rankings despite low momentum include Pharmaceutical Retailers (+9 spots, momentum 0.44), Insurance - Diversified (+8 spots, momentum 0.49), and Aerospace & Defense (+7 spots, momentum 0.40).

pulse.headline: Uranium and coal lead gains amid weak overall market breadth.

conviction.why: Conviction is low due to a weak 19% all-green breadth and five fading divergences, despite a 0.66 mean rank agreement.
